classification.difficultyReason: The supplied radius–height relationship and part a expressions scaffold substitution, Pythagoras and reversing the volume formula; part b requires recognising that the water forms a similar cone.

content.prompt: The cone shown in this diagram has an open circular top of radius $r$ cm and depth $h$ cm. The radius of the cone is equal to one-third of the height; that is, $r=\dfrac{h}{3}$.

spec.description: Unshaded inverted open cone, complete solid top ellipse, centre-to-rim radius and external vertical depth dimension. Ordinary source blue strokes and red centre marker are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: Right circular cone with radius r and perpendicular depth h; r=h/3.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied r and h labels are visible.

answer.short:
$A=\sqrt{10}\pi r^2$

Use the curved surface only because the top is open.
answer.worked:
Let $\ell$ be the slant height. By Pythagoras’ theorem,
$$\begin{align*}\ell^2&=r^2+(3r)^2\\\ell^2&=10r^2\\\ell&=r\sqrt{10}\end{align*}$$
The open cone has only a curved surface:
$$\begin{align*}A&=\pi r\ell\\A&=\pi r(r\sqrt{10})\\A&=\sqrt{10}\pi r^2\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: If the cone holds $50\text{ cm}^3$ of water, find:

children.label: i
children.prompt: the depth of water in the cone, correct to three significant figures

answer.worked:
The water forms a similar cone, so its radius and depth also satisfy $h=3r$.
$$\begin{align*}V&=\pi r^3\\50&=\pi r^3\\r&=\sqrt[3]{\frac{50}{\pi}}\\h&=3\sqrt[3]{\frac{50}{\pi}}\\h&\approx7.55\text{ cm}\quad\text{(3 s.f.)}\end{align*}$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: the curved surface area of the cone covered by water, correct to three significant figures

answer.worked:
Use the unrounded water radius from part b(i).
$$\begin{align*}A&=\sqrt{10}\pi r^2\\A&=\sqrt{10}\pi\left(\sqrt[3]{\frac{50}{\pi}}\right)^2\\A&\approx62.9\text{ cm}^2\quad\text{(3 s.f.)}\end{align*}$$
